page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc8i.8xlarge is a compute-focused instance within the high clock speed family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. The system delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs running on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6462C processor with a base clock frequency of 3.3 GHz. Memory capacity is provisioned at 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per dedicated core.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 32 Gbps for sustained traffic. The server configuration includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for operating system disks and persistent file storage. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs present, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

By maintaining a dense 1:2 memory-to-core profile, the instance optimizes expenditure for pure processing pipelines by avoiding unneeded memory capacity. The primary hardware tradeoff is the total reliance on external storage and limited RAM headroom for memory-heavy datasets. Workloads that match this profile include software compilation pipelines, batch computing, CI/CD runners, distributed application services, and compute-heavy mathematical modeling.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance from the high clock speed family, running on KVM virtualization. The system is equipped with 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6462C processor running at 3.3 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM at 2.0 GB per vCPU. Networking throughput operates at a baseline of 32 Gbps. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations, and includes no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With a compute-focused 1:2 processor-to-memory balance, ecs.hfc8i.8xlarge provides dense processing power for CPU-bound tasks while avoiding the expense of surplus memory. This hardware profile aligns with compute-intensive workloads such as code compilation, automated CI/CD builds, batch data processing, and clustered application web serving that demand sustained high clock frequencies without large memory footprints.
